title: Pairwise signal matrix and decision notes — May 2025
body:
Purpose and context:

This is the working decision memo for the May 2025 model onboarding run focused on pairwise signal analysis rather than a single aggregate leaderboard score. The goal: pick a default production model variant for hosted inference for the customer-support vertical while capturing precise failure modes and an "edge-case ledger" for future tuning.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Recommend pilot rollout of redwood-xxl-1.1-qat as the primary candidate for hosted+dedicated tiers.
- Keep redwood-xxl-1.0 in warm fallback for highest-fidelity responses for a 5% canary at start.
- Defer full rollout of redwood-quant-8bit-1.1 until follow-up regressions pass (see rollback criteria).

Why pairwise?
- Aggregate leaderboards hide head-to-head tradeoffs (e.g., A is better on QA but worse on code examples).
- Pairwise matrices make tie-breakers explicit and are better for small but high-impact slices.

Datasets used (short):
- core-promptset-v3: 1,200 prompts (user-support focused, multi-turn preserved)
- synthetic-adversarial-v1: 450 adversarial/paraphrase attacks (hallucination triggers)
- regression-holdouts-q2: 300 historical tickets with annotated preferred outputs
- latency-simulated: 10k sampled tokens with seq length distribution matching production

Models compared (short names):
- A: redwood-xxl-1.0 (baseline)
- B: redwood-xxl-1.1-qat (quant-aware training + 4-bit friendly)
- C: redwood-quant-8bit-1.1 (8-bit quantized variant)
- D: open-llama-70b-v2 (external open-model baseline)

Pairwise win/loss snapshot (summary counts over core-promptset-v3, n=1200):
- A vs B: B wins 722, A wins 428 (B net +294)
- B vs C: B wins 610, C wins 430, ties 160 (B net +180)
- A vs C: A wins 534, C wins 466 (A net +68)
- B vs D: B wins 780, D wins 420 (B net +360)
- C vs D: C wins 400, D wins 560 (D net +160)

Interpretation notes:
- B (xxl-1.1-qat) consistently beats A on customer-support phrasing, clarification prompts, and multi-turn context preservation.
- C (8bit) loses to B more often on subtle intent distinctions (we believe quantization noise is the cause) but beats D on latency and cost.
- D (open-llama) shows strength on short factual lookups but regresses heavily on conversational continuity.

Per-slice breakdown highlights (selected):
- Escalation prompts (n=220): B > A by +48% win rate; C underperforms B by -22%.
- Sensitive entity-handling (PII redaction scenarios, n=110): A edges B slightly (A +6 wins) — reason: conservative output truncation heuristics in A retained after training; B increased helpfulness but occasionally provided riskier surface-level answers.
- Multimodal proxy prompts (code snippets in text, n=80): C slightly outperforms A (C +9) likely due to kernel-level optimizations in the quantized path.

Quality metrics (averages across core-promptset-v3):
- Helpfulness (human score 1-5): A=3.6, B=4.1, C=3.8, D=3.4
- Hallucination rate (annotator-labeled): A=7.2%, B=8.5%, C=9.0%, D=12.8%
- Latency median (ms per response, simulated): A=420ms, B=310ms, C=190ms, D=660ms
- Cost per 1k tokens (relative units): A=1.00, B=0.78, C=0.45, D=0.65

Edge-case ledger (examples to track and fix):
- EC-01: B truncates policy links when long parentheses are present; appears to be tokenization + post-processing bug. Repro: prompt id core-00427. Action: file bug to serving-runtime with minimal repro.
- EC-02: C hallucinates nonexistent KB IDs when prompt contains code fences; repro in synthetic-adversarial-092. Likely quantization instability in attention scaling; escalate to applied-ml research.
- EC-03: D gives inconsistent customer-tone across turns (flips to terse) — expected for open baseline, not acceptable for default.

Tie-breaker heuristics we used when pairwise wins were close:
1) Favor lower latency if win margin < 5% and hallucination delta < 1.5pp.
2) Favor lower cost if stability (std dev helpfulness) difference < 0.05.
3) For PII/safety slices, favor conservative output (even if helpfulness drops up to 0.2 points).

Rollout plan (recommended):
- Week 0 (canary): Deploy B to 5% of hosted traffic for customer-support route. Keep A as fallback for requests with safety flags. Monitor: hallucination rate, escalation false positives, latency, and user satisfaction signal (NPS micro).
- Week 2 (expand): If no regression in slice metrics and overall hallucination delta < +1.0pp, expand to 30%.
- Week 4 (standard): Expand to 100% for hosted standard tier and deploy C to Dedicated-light nodes where extreme cost sensitivity is configured, but mark C as "best-effort" and route high-sensitivity prompts to B.

Rollback criteria (immediate revert to baseline A if any of the following for a sustained 24-hour window on canary traffic):
- Hallucination rate increase > +3.0 percentage points absolute.
- Escalation false positive rate increases > +12% relative.
- Critical PII/safety violations >= 2 confirmed incidents (manual review) in 24 hours.

Open action items (owners):
- Aisha: create minimal repro for EC-01 and open issue in serving-runtime (due 2025-05-18).
- Liam: run follow-up 8-bit stability experiments with quant-noise ablation and share results (due 2025-05-25).
- Sofia: wire a synthetic monitoring probe for the PII slice into Console dashboards (due 2025-05-20).
- Noah: prepare suggested canary routing config and percentage rollout feature flag PR (due 2025-05-19).

Notes on evaluation methodology differences vs previous runs:
- This run prioritized human pairwise judgments (A/B preference) over automatic metrics when available; annotator inter-rater agreement was Cohen's kappa=0.71.
- We introduced synthetic-adversarial-v1 to stress hallucination behaviors specifically for quantized variants.

Questions for review:
- Are we comfortable with B's small bump in hallucinations (+1.3pp vs A) in exchange for large gains in helpfulness and latency?
- Should we accelerate C into Dedicated-light earlier for customers with strict cost controls?
- Do we want an additional micro-canary specifically for PII-sensitive routes running only A until EC-01 is resolved?

Appendix (quick links and artifacts):
- Full pairwise matrix CSV (attached to this Drive doc): /attachments/pairwise-matrix-may2025.csv (internal)
- Annotator schema and quality control notes: CONFLUENCE-ML-1279
- Benchmark run CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-benchmarks/actions/runs/34567

End of memo. Please add comments inline for any disagreements; we'll finalize by EOD 2025-05-21 for routing to product and SRE for the canary config."
